messages:

Subject: Cascade - clarify monthly tokens and concurrency targets

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can finalize a hosted pricing band for you. Attachment: cascade_mau_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet) + redwood-proposal-v0.3.pdf (proposal draft).

Key points I captured:
- Workload shape: chat-first assistant with average 1.8 prompts per session and avg prompt size ~450 tokens. Average model output ~650 tokens.
- Current expected monthly active users: ~120k; you estimated monthly tokens broadly in the 50M–90M range depending on rollout cadence.
- Traffic spikes: product launches and promotions could create short bursts. You mentioned a peak TPS observed in prototype runs ~200–250 TPS for ~10–15 minute windows.
- Budget target: you indicated a target around $900–$1,000 per 1M tokens (total spend target, not per-call).

Open questions for confirmation (these will materially affect unit pricing):
1) Please confirm the working range you expect to commit to for the next 3 months: baseline monthly tokens vs expected ramp vs max-month spike. Example format: baseline / expected / spike (e.g., 30M / 65M / 120M).
2) Are embeddings part of this traffic, or is this strictly generation (chat/completions)? If embeddings, roughly what proportion (%)?
3) For burst handling: is the 200–250 TPS an observed short burst (1–30 min) or sustained for hours? We price sustained capacity and short burst capacity differently.
4) Any procurement timeline or PO threshold we should be aware of?

Proposed next steps: if you confirm the numbers above, we’ll produce a 2-option hosted quote: a consumption-first band with soft volume discounts and an annual committed band with lower $/1M and reserved burst capacity.

Thanks — I’m aiming to have draft bands ready by Monday if we can lock the token ranges this week.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Hi Jonas — thanks for the detailed recap. Confirming numbers from our side: 

Baseline / Expected / Spike (next 3 months): 45M / 68M / 140M tokens. The spike number reflects a worst-case promotional launch we run quarterly; typical spikes have been 10–20 minutes but last quarter’s experiment held ~35 minutes at ~120 TPS.

Embeddings: not included in these figures — embeddings are a separate pipeline (we'll exclude that for the initial contract).

Peak TPS: prototype runs peaked at ~220 TPS sustained for short bursts (10–35 minutes). For capacity planning, please assume burst windows up to 45 minutes during a launch.

Budget target: we are aiming to keep hosted spend to ~ $900 / 1M tokens (all-in target). If committed pricing can get significantly below that we can discuss a larger commit.

Procurement timeline: we have a procurement review on 2028-05-25. Procurement contact is procurement@cascade.ai — they will need an SOW + pricing sheet + SOC2 evidence (we have your SOC2 in our portal).

I attached our internal traffic slice (op-model.xlsx) for reference.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of Product, Cascade AI

Sarah — perfect, this is very helpful. Two quick clarifications and a preliminary band suggestion. Quoting your note below as context.

> Baseline / Expected / Spike (next 3 months): 45M / 68M / 140M tokens.
> Peak TPS: prototype runs peaked at ~220 TPS sustained for short bursts (10–35 minutes). Burst windows up to 45 minutes.
> Embeddings: not included.
> Budget target: ~$900 / 1M tokens.

Clarifications: 
- When you say "sustained for short bursts (10–35 minutes)" — is the 220 TPS measured as 95th percentile over that window, or a raw instantaneous peak? Our billing and capacity planning treat 95th-percentile sustained concurrency differently than instantaneous micro-peaks.
- Do you expect any concurrent internal admin or ML pipeline calls that hit the same endpoint during launches (those add to sustained load)?

Preliminary hosted bands (consumption, not committed) — ballpark for discussion only: 
- Band A (consumption, no commit): $1,050 / 1M tokens baseline, with burst premium for sustained windows > 15 minutes.
- Band B (12-month commit, volume tiered): starts $820 / 1M at 60M/mo committed, steps down to $720 / 1M at 100M/mo committed; includes 30 minutes per-day burst allowance and lower surge fees for short spikes.

If 220 TPS is a 95th percentile across the burst window, Band B would be the clearly better commercial fit; if that 220 TPS is an instantaneous peak but the 95th is much lower, we can probably keep Band A as-is and not charge sustained burst premiums.

I'll draft both options into the proposal and include explicit definitions for "sustained burst" vs "instantaneous peak" so procurement can map to internal SLAs. Marissa — can you and Karthik take the pricing bands and produce a one-page pricing sheet we can share with procurement next week?

Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
